caption: Meet Rachel
text: Meet Rachel. She runs a 100-room hotel in Chicago.

caption: It's a January night, and the heating is running
text: Right now, it's a January night, and the heating is running.

caption: Press play: night, morning, summer, winter
text: Press play, and the whole year runs: night and morning, winter and summer, every hour of it.

caption: Same hotel, six months later: now cooling does the work
text: Same hotel, six months later. Now cooling is doing the work.

caption: Bookings are climbing from 60% to 85%
text: Bookings are climbing from sixty to eighty-five percent, and her owner wants the bill kept in check.

caption: $50,000. A recommendation by Friday.
text: He gives her fifty thousand dollars and wants a recommendation by Friday. Solar? LEDs? Smart room controls? What would you buy?

caption: $5.2 billion a year
text: US hotels spend about five point two billion dollars a year on energy.

caption: Try it on a virtual hotel first
text: Energy Twin lets her try those decisions on a virtual hotel first.

caption: "Where is my hotel spending the most on energy?"
text: Rachel starts with a question: where is my hotel spending the most on energy? The briefing points her toward the biggest loads.

caption: Follow the cost from electricity and gas to the systems and spaces using it
text: In the twin, she can follow the cost from electricity and gas to the systems and spaces using them.

caption: She asks the advisor
text: She asks: at eighty-five percent, what if we turn on smart room controls?

caption: The engine runs the what-if; the advisor explains it
text: The advisor asks the engine to run the what-if, and explains the result. Every number comes from the model.

caption: Before and after, side by side
text: On one side, the hotel today. On the other, empty rooms are set back automatically.

caption: Now let's spend her $50,000
text: Now let's spend her fifty thousand dollars.

caption: Top pick: LEDs plus occupancy sensors
text: The winner: LEDs plus occupancy sensors. About thirty-nine thousand dollars, saving ten thousand three hundred a year, paid back in three point eight years.

caption: Remember your vote? Ask why this package came out ahead
text: Remember what you voted for? Let's ask the advisor why this package came out ahead.

caption: Does it still win when we stress-test the assumptions?
text: And does it still win when we stress-test the assumptions, like electricity prices going up twenty percent?

caption: On Friday: a recommendation with the projected savings and every assumption behind them
text: On Friday, she brings her owner the recommendation and every assumption behind it.

caption: "I own ten hotels."
text: He looks at it and asks: I own ten hotels. If I have another fifty thousand for the whole group, where should it go?

caption: One budget, split across the group
text: Energy Twin splits one budget across the group, and shows what each selected hotel would buy.

caption: Next: one real hotel
text: With a real customer, we'd start with one hotel, its bills and real quotes, then check the savings against the bills.

caption: Simulate smarter. Spend better. Save energy.
text: Energy Twin. Simulate smarter. Spend better. Save energy.
